assignments.reason: Yom Kippur is the sacred day on which God forgave Israel and said 'סָלַחְתִּי כִּדְבָרֶיךָ', after which His Name was enlarged and revealed. The Torah explicitly states that after Yom Kippur 'נִתְגַּלָּה בְּחִינַת שֵׁם ה'' and that is why the day after Yom Kippur is called 'שֵׁם ה''. Yom Kippur's essential nature in this Torah is the moment of reconciliation that restores and magnifies the Divine Name — placing it squarely in the domain of the Name and life-force.

This node — 'the aspect of God's Name was revealed' — is the revelation of the Divine Name itself. Its essential nature IS the Name of God becoming manifest. It directly describes the state of שם ה' being present and accessible, which is the core concept of Package 1.

Coming to the Tzaddik and seeing him is an activity whose essential nature belongs to the domain of the Tzaddik. The Torah frames this through the verse 'וְהָיוּ עֵינֶיךָ רֹאוֹת אֶת מוֹרֶיךָ', whose initial letters spell אש רוח מים עפר (the four elements) — because the Tzaddik IS the Simple Foundation from which these elements flow. Seeing the Tzaddik is encountering the יסוד הפשוט directly.

assignments.reason: Finding oneself within the Tzaddik and examining one's character traits is essentially about the Tzaddik as the root-source of all middot. The Torah explains that all middot flow from the four elements, which in turn flow from the Tzaddik (the Simple Foundation). This self-examination through the Tzaddik is an expression of the Tzaddik's nature as the unified root of all traits — its essential nature belongs to the Tzaddik/יסוד הפשוט domain.
